mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5 percentage points over the past month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 60-day rolling mean during the same period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a 6-month window, it triggers a risk premium increase on equities, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% in a 6-month window
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the 30-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS labor cost growth above 3% signals wage inflation that outpaces productivity, raising the real wage premium and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows by more than 3% month-over-month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 personal consumption turns up by more than 6% from the prior quarter, it indicates strong consumer demand that boosts corporate earnings expectations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below 100 (deflationary pressure) reduces business confidence and elevates the cost of capital, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 3 consecutive months below 100
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (wage growth and unemployment rate both rising) create a labor market tension that raises risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: Both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS near 0%, the lack of policy tightening supports risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly RSAFS inventory drawdown exceeds 10% of the prior month's level, it indicates overproduction in the supply chain and reduces future demand expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS drawdown > 10% of previous month's value
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the 30-day prior window (t-test p > 0.05).
